# Copilot / AI agent instructions for Windows-Hinting

These instructions apply to all AI coding agents (GitHub Copilot chat, Copilot
coding agent, Cursor, Claude, etc.) working in this repository.

## Building

Everything builds with the .NET 10 SDK pinned by `global.json` (stable SDKs
only); Visual Studio is optional. The solution is `Windows-Hinting.slnx`.

```pwsh
dotnet build .\Windows-Hinting\Windows-Hinting.csproj -c Debug
```

For release-style outputs run `build/build-complete.ps1` with PowerShell 7
(`pwsh`), the same script CI calls (`Get-Help .\build\build-complete.ps1` lists
the switches):

- `-Configuration Release` builds the exe and the MSI; `-ExeOnly` skips the
  MSI; `-InstallerOnly` packages the MSI from the existing app output without
  rebuilding it (CI signs the binaries in between).
- `-Portable [-Runtime win-x64|win-x86|all]` publishes the self-contained
  single-file exes. Their settings live in
  `Windows-Hinting/Properties/PublishProfiles/Portable-win-*.pubxml`, so
  `dotnet publish -p:PublishProfile=Portable-win-x64` and Visual Studio's
  Publish produce the same output.

Rules that are easy to break:

- Settings that depend on `PortableBuild` (the `PORTABLE` define, the manifest
  choice) belong in `Windows-Hinting/Directory.Build.targets`, not the csproj:
  publish profiles are imported after the project body.
- The MSI harvests the app's build output with a WiX `<Files>` element
  (`Windows-Hinting.Installer/Components.wxs`), so new dependencies are picked
  up automatically. Don't list files by hand.
- NuGet packages are locked (`packages.lock.json` per project) and CI restores in
  locked mode, so run `dotnet restore` and commit the updated lock files after
  adding or changing a `PackageReference`. Portable publishes are the exception
  (see `Windows-Hinting/Directory.Build.targets`). The NetSparkle AppCastGenerator
  version is pinned in `dotnet-tools.json`.
- Code-signing and release secrets live in GitHub Environments (`signing` /
  `release` for main, `signing-branch` / `release-branch` with required approval for
  other branches) and are used only by the `sign-binaries`, `sign-msi` and `release`
  jobs. The signing jobs check out no code and the release job builds nothing; never
  reference these secrets from a job that runs a build. Published releases are always
  signed: a manual run with `publish_release` but not `sign_binaries` fails.
- Formatting is enforced by pre-commit (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`). Run
  `pre-commit install` once so hooks fix files at commit time, or
  `pre-commit run --all-files`. CI runs the same hooks first and only builds once they
  pass; on pull requests pre-commit.ci lite commits any fixes back to the PR (`style:
  apply pre-commit fixes`), which then builds. Pull that commit before pushing again.

## Other project conventions

- Target framework is `net10.0-windows`.
- Nullability is enabled project-wide — keep new code null-safe.
- Native interop is generated by **CsWin32** from
  `Windows-Hinting/NativeMethods.txt`. When you need a new Win32 API, add it to
  that file and use `Windows.Win32.PInvoke.*` — do not add hand-written
  `[DllImport]` declarations.
- UI Automation is generated by CsWin32 too (`Windows.Win32.UI.Accessibility`,
  "Wave 7" in `NativeMethods.txt`): add any new `IUIAutomation*` interface
  there. Use the `UIA_PROPERTY_ID` / `UIA_PATTERN_ID` / `UIA_CONTROLTYPE_ID`
  enums for IDs. The generated `Cached*`/`Current*` string properties return
  raw `BSTR`s the caller must free, so read strings through
  `UIAutomationElementExtensions` (or `Get*PropertyValue(...) as string`)
  instead. Do not reintroduce the `UIAutomationClient` tlbimp reference.
- Per-monitor DPI is `PerMonitorV2` (manifest + csproj); overlays are one
  WinForms form per `Screen`. Do not introduce a single spanning overlay HWND.
- Verification is manual — there are no automated tests. After changes, rebuild
  in VS and confirm: hotkeys fire, hints render on primary + secondary monitors,
  mouse clicks route correctly, and display-change rebuilds overlays.
